edits.old: The parameters and reference data the run reads are the rwb-case contracts (DP-06, DP-07), the topic and event names come from the naming library (DP-14), the schema objects arrive through the P1 Flyway sequence (DP-15) and the account and arrears facts come from the ACE views read by rwb-source-data alone (DP-05). The target read operation by which rwb-case serves the list that rwb-source-data builds is `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases` and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases` on the rwb-case base, and the daily extract reaches rwb-reporting through the rwb-integration activity `deliverFile` on queue `rwb-integration` with a manifest of fileId, batchId, sha256 and record count, with `rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1` and `rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1` on `rwb.integration.events.v1` and no data lake path (GAP-0335, resolved at the wave-1 contract review).
edits.new: The parameters and reference data the run reads are the rwb-case contracts (DP-06, DP-07), the topic and event names come from the naming library (DP-14), the schema objects arrive through the P1 Flyway sequence (DP-15) and the account and arrears facts come from the ACE views read by rwb-source-data alone (DP-05). What no source states is the target read operation by which rwb-case serves the list that rwb-source-data builds, and how the daily extract reaches rwb-reporting once the data lake is removed: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0335; ASM-0429). The story proves the two operations that exist today and records the choice as an assumption, so a change of operation is one contract edit and one test change.
